brings happiness, prosperity and good health to everyone.  
Heritage Foods delivered a strong performance in quarter 2 of this financial year, 
sustaining revenue growth despite an inflationary environment marked by rising 
milk procurement costs and supply side constraints.  
Consolidated revenue grew 19% year-on-year to INR13,196 million in quarter 2, 
taking H1 revenue to INR26,577 million, up 18%. While elevated procurement 
costs continue to weigh on profitability, EBITDA stood at INR740 million with a 
margin of 5.6% and profit after tax was INR309 million. Encouragingly, EBITDA

margin improved by 98 basis points sequentially over Q1 of this financial year, 
reflecting a recovery in operating performance amid sustained cost pressures. 
Our integrated farm-to-consumer model underpins our ability to ensure reliable 
milk availability, strengthen farmer relationships and respond to evolving 
consumer preferences. During the quarter, we continued to build on this 
foundation through a stronger procurement network, expansion of our value-
added products portfolio and investments in premium and nutrition-led 
categories.  
A strong and resilient procurement network remains fundamental to our 
business. During Q2, milk procurement volumes increased 7% year-on-year to 
17.28 lakh liters per day, while H1 procurement volumes grew 4% to 17,69,000 
liters per day. This growth, despite monsoon-related supply constraints, reflects 
our sustained efforts to deepen our village level procurement network and 
strengthen farmer engagement.  
At the same time, milk procurement inflation remains elevated across the 
country. Our average landed milk procurement cost increased 11% year-on-year 
to INR47.73 per liter in quarter 2, driven by sustained demand, limited 
improvement in milk arrivals and higher feed and fodder costs. These pressures 
continue to weigh on near-term profitability across the dairy industry, making 
procurement efficiency and calibrated pricing critical. 
On the consumer side, our core milk business continued to demonstrate 
strength of the Heritage brand and sustained consumer trust. Milk sales 
volumes increased 2% year-on-year to 12.35 lakh liters per day in Q2, while 
average selling prices improved 6% to INR60.34 per liter. For H1, milk sales 
volume grew at 1% to 11.99 lakh liters per day, while average selling prices 
increased 5% to INR59.54 per liter. Our focus remains on balancing volume 
growth with calibrated pricing while protecting the strength of our consumer 
franchise. 
The evolution of our business mix continues to be an important driver of 
Heritage's growth. Value-added products remain a key growth engine with 
revenue, excluding ghee and butter, increasing 32% year-on-year to INR4,510 
million in Q2 and 36% to INR10,146 million in H1 of this year. Consequently, 
VAP contribution increased to 35.4% of revenue in Q2 from 31.3% in the 
corresponding quarter last year and to 39.6% in H1 from 33.7% in H1 of last 
year.

Growth was broad-based across categories, led by lassi, buttermilk, ice cream,

more diversified and premium branded dairy business. We believe this shift will 
strengthen consumer loyalty, improve product differentiation and support 
earnings resilience over time. 
Alongside portfolio expansion, we continue to invest in innovation. During the 
quarter, we strengthened our high protein portfolio with the launch of Nourish+ 
High Protein Curd containing 25 grams of protein and Greek Yogurt available in 
single-serve packs containing 8 grams of protein and midsized packs containing 
40 grams of protein.  
We also expanded the Alpenvie ice cream range and introduced organic curd, 
further strengthening our presence across premium dairy segments. Our 
objective is to build differentiated products that address emerging consumer 
needs while leveraging our brands, manufacturing capabilities and distribution 
network. These initiatives are helping us expand our presence in premium dairy 
and nutrition-led categories with attractive long-term growth potential. 
We continue to strengthen our adjacent growth platforms during the quarter. 
The newly commissioned ice cream facility provides additional manufacturing 
capacity for Alpenvie and Get-A-Way, supporting capacity absorption, operating 
leverage and future growth. Get-A-Way in which we now hold 71% stake 
delivered robust revenue growth during the quarter with Heritage manufacturing 
and supplying 3,272 liters of ice cream per day to support its growth, its product 
availability and expansion.

growth.
